name: BC517
description: NPN Darlington (two cascaded NPN transistors in one TO-92) with very high current gain (hFE >= 30000). Logic-level drive of relays, LEDs, small motors up to about 1A. C-B-E pinout, the European TO-92 layout.

TO-92.notes: flat face toward you, leads down: C-B-E. Opposite of the 2N3904 (E-B-C).

extra.type: Darlington (plain 2-transistor, no internal base-emitter shunt resistors or clamp diode)

typical_application: High-gain low-power switching from a microcontroller or logic pin: relay, LED, and small-motor drive needing very little base current.
gotchas: C-B-E pin order, not the E-B-C of common US TO-92 parts; easy to insert backwards
Darlington Vbe(on) is high (up to ~1.4V, two junctions) and Vce(sat) up to ~1.0V at 100mA; it never saturates as low as a single BJT, so it dissipates more as a switch
no internal flyback/clamp diode; add one externally for inductive loads
huge hFE means tiny base current; leakage can turn it on, consider an external base-emitter resistor in hot or high-impedance designs
